title: Toilet (tank, fill valve, flapper, base)

parts.label: Toilet
parts.looks: Bowl on the floor with a tank behind it and a handle on the tank.
parts.normal: Fills and stops within about a minute after a flush; no water on the floor.
parts.abnormal: Water still running into the bowl long after a flush, or water on the floor around the base.

parts.label: Tank (lid off)
parts.looks: The box behind the seat; with the lid off you see the fill valve on one side and the flush valve in the middle.
parts.normal: Water level steady, about an inch below the top of the overflow tube.
parts.abnormal: Water spilling into the overflow tube, or the level dropping by itself.

parts.label: Fill valve
parts.looks: The tall plastic column on the left of the tank with a float cup or a float ball on an arm.
parts.normal: Stops filling when the float rises; silent once full.
parts.abnormal: Keeps hissing or whistling, or fills past the overflow tube.

parts.label: Flapper
parts.looks: The rubber cap at the bottom of the tank, over the drain hole, lifted by a chain from the handle.
parts.normal: Sits flat and seals; chain has a little slack.
parts.abnormal: Warped, slimy or cracked rubber, a chain too tight to let it close, or it closes crooked.

parts.label: Overflow tube
parts.looks: The open pipe standing up in the middle of the tank, next to the flapper.
parts.abnormal: Water pouring into its top (fill level set too high or a fill valve that will not shut).

parts.label: Supply line and stop valve
parts.looks: The small valve on the wall or floor behind the toilet, left side, and the flexible line up to the tank.
parts.abnormal: Drips at the nut or valve stem, a bulging or rusty line.

parts.label: Base and floor
parts.looks: Where the bowl meets the floor, with two bolt caps on the sides.
parts.normal: Dry floor; the toilet does not move when pushed gently.
parts.abnormal: Water seeping out at the base after a flush, stained or soft flooring, or the toilet rocks.

faults.name: Flapper not sealing (running toilet, phantom flush)
faults.evidence: Water trickling into the bowl with the level dropping, or the tank refilling by itself every few minutes; a few drops of food colouring in the tank show in the bowl within 15 minutes without flushing.

faults.name: Fill valve not shutting off (hissing or whistling)
faults.evidence: Hissing or whistling that goes on after the tank is full, with water running into the overflow tube.

faults.name: Water level set too high
faults.evidence: Water running into the overflow tube while the fill valve is otherwise working; the float sits high on its column.

faults.name: Chain too short or tangled
faults.evidence: Flapper held slightly open by a tight chain, seen with the lid off.

faults.name: Failed wax ring at the base
faults.evidence: Water at the base after a flush (not condensation), or the toilet rocking when pushed gently.

faults.name: Supply line or stop valve leak
faults.evidence: Drops forming at the line's nut or the valve stem, seen with light.

faults.name: Partial clog or blocked vent (gurgling, weak flush)
faults.evidence: Bowl water level rising high then draining slowly, or gurgling in this toilet when another fixture drains; a noise alone is a description, not proof.

hazards.label: Water reaching electrics
hazards.threshold: Standing water on the floor visibly touching an outlet, a power strip, a cord or an electric heater.

may: Lift the tank lid and set it down flat on a towel to look inside.
With the lid off, flush once and keep the camera on the open tank until it stops refilling.
Close the stop valve behind the toilet by turning it clockwise (water only), then flush once to empty the tank.
Put a few drops of food colouring in the tank and wait 15 minutes without flushing.
Describe the noise in words: hissing, whistling, gurgling, banging, or a refill every few minutes.
must_not: Use a chemical drain cleaner in a toilet.
Stand on the toilet or the tank.

tour.open: Show me the whole toilet and the floor around it from about a metre back. Next I'll ask you to lift the tank lid so I can watch it work.

checkpoints.hint: Lift the tank lid, set it flat on a towel, and point the camera straight into the tank. Then flush once, tap Listen to it, and keep the phone over the tank while it refills, so I can watch the flapper close and hear whether the water stops.
Look behind the toilet on the left, low down, for the small valve and the line going up to the tank.
Point at the floor where the bowl meets it. Tap Light if it is dark.
